hints: Notice the starting values: fringe width $12 \text{ mm}$ with $D = 2.4 \text{ m}$ and $a = 0.10 \text{ mm}$, changing to $D = 1.8 \text{ m}$ with doubled $a$.
Recall fringe width $w = \lambda D / a$ for double-slit interference, with wavelength $\lambda$ unchanged because the light is still monochromatic.
Use ratios to avoid finding $\lambda$: multiply $12 \text{ mm}$ by $1.8/2.4$ for the $D$ change and by $1/2$ for the doubled $a$.
walkthrough: Identify the useful data: initial width $w = 12 \text{ mm}$, initial $D = 2.4 \text{ m}$, final $D = 1.8 \text{ m}$, and final slit separation $a$ is $2$ times the initial $a$.
State the governing rule: double-slit fringe width is $w = \lambda D / a$, so for fixed $\lambda$, $w$ is directly proportional to $D$ and inversely proportional to $a$.
Set up a ratio so $\lambda$ cancels: $w_{new} = w_{old} \times (D_{new}/D_{old}) \times (a_{old}/a_{new})$.
Substitute values with units: $w_{new} = 12 \text{ mm} \times (1.8 \text{ m} / 2.4 \text{ m}) \times (1/2) = 12 \text{ mm} \times 0.75 \times 0.5$.
Calculate the intermediate result: $12 \text{ mm} \times 0.75 = 9.0 \text{ mm}$, then $9.0 \text{ mm} \times 0.5 = 4.5 \text{ mm}$, which has the correct unit of length. This is option B

options.A: Too small. It would require dividing by 8, for example halving $D$ as well as doubling $a$ twice.
options.B: Fringe width scales as $D/a$, so $12 \text{ mm} \times (1.8/2.4) \times (1/2) = 4.5 \text{ mm}$.
options.C: This is half the original $12 \text{ mm}$ and accounts only for doubling $a$, ignoring the change of $D$ from $2.4 \text{ m}$ to $1.8 \text{ m}$.
options.D: This accounts only for reducing $D$ by factor $1.8/2.4$, ignoring that doubling slit separation $a$ halves the fringe width.
